rationale: AsyncMock records a call when its coroutine is constructed. A called-only assertion does not establish that the required submission was awaited. Preserve the caller contract and repair the assertion.
The declared boundary is the caller awaiting the dependency, not remote delivery. The await assertion rejects a caller that merely constructs the coroutine.
A type annotation does not prevent invalid runtime input. This is a public normalization boundary whose ValueError behavior is independently specified and tested.

The only application call constructs a validated _Request before reaching _route. Its None and dict accommodation branches serve no public contract in this closed fixture. Preserve the actual validation in _normalize.

The fixture commits the expected row before save. A no-op save passes this assertion. The adjacent cold-connection test retains new-account persistence coverage, but update semantics would require separate evidence.
The row is absent initially and read through a separate connection after the owner returns. A no-op save is rejected without a mocked persistence boundary.

The document does not exist, so the authorization branch is never reached. Bypassing ownership leaves this check green. It may be relabeled as missing-record coverage; retain the existing-record denial check.
The document exists and only ownership is wrong. Bypassing the ownership guard changes the result and deletes the row, which the unchanged test rejects.
The advertised capability inventory is itself a documented public compatibility contract. The test claims discovery, not execution of a scheduling operation.
The clock is an explicit public dependency boundary with a production default. Its only local override being a test does not make it dead scaffolding or rule out external users.
Both expected and actual depend on total. Changing the fee to seven percent moves both sides and passes. The adjacent independent amount check rejects this mutation.
The literal expected amount is independently derived from the stated fee contract and rejects a changed fee factor.
